claims.text: The feedstock is a cobalt-free Al-Cr-Fe-Ni-Si high-entropy-alloy powder.
The powder bed and substrate should be maintained at 300–500°C during laser powder bed fusion.
In situ powder-bed preheating reduces thermal gradients during melting and solidification.
Reduced cooling rates and thermal gradients minimize heterogeneous nucleation and rapid quenching.
Heterogeneous nucleation and rapid quenching normally trigger phase segregation and defect formation.
Preheating produces a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Preheating reduces segregation defects in laser-powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating reduces residual thermal-stress buildup in laser-powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower residual stress and a more uniform microstructure enhance mechanical integrity.
Preheated builds will exhibit a statistically significant improvement of more than 10% in yield strength relative to non-preheated laser powder bed fusion builds.
Preheated builds will exhibit a statistically significant improvement of more than 10% in ductility relative to non-preheated laser powder bed fusion builds.
Preheated builds will have lower X-ray-diffraction-measured residual stresses than non-preheated builds.
Preheated builds will contain fewer microstructural defects than non-preheated builds.
Preheated builds will show fewer segregation features than non-preheated builds.
Conventional laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without preheating is known to exhibit segregation, high residual stresses, and defect formation.
The proposed effects may not translate directly to other manufacturing methods or systems with significantly different thermal properties.
